title: P2P Back-Office Admin Platform
subtitle: Built and hardened the internal admin system used to manage users, loans, KYC, and compliance for a regulated P2P lending platform
company: A Bank of Thailand-regulated P2P lending platform

timeline.description: Built out core admin screens for contracts, StockLend matching, and investor re-KYC workflows — including juristic/corporate re-KYC — on top of the existing Django admin
Closed a dual-approval bypass in the KYC approval flow and added an atomic transaction lock to remove a race condition that let two approvers process the same case simultaneously

Replaced scattered permission checks with a data-driven Role Permission Matrix enforced server-side, then built an immutable Audit Trail instrumented across login, role changes, and every back-office action
Shipped the Close User Account workflow and a new eKYC/IT-Biometrics accuracy reporting system (FAR/FRR metrics, dynamic Word reports) for compliance review

challenges.title: Permissions and audit history weren't first-class concepts
challenges.description: Early admin screens relied on Django's built-in admin and ad-hoc permission checks, with no way to see who took a sensitive action or reconstruct why

challenges.title: A dual-approval workflow could still be raced
challenges.description: KYC approval required two approvers by design, but nothing stopped both approvals from landing on the same case at once, opening a bypass

challenges.title: Compliance reporting was manual
challenges.description: Biometric accuracy (FAR/FRR) and eKYC figures had to be compiled by hand for regulatory review, with no self-serve reporting for the compliance team

solutions.category: Permissions and audit history weren't first-class concepts
items: Modeled a Role Permission Matrix (role × feature × action) as data, enforced server-side for both UI visibility and view logic
Built an AuditTrail model with an immutability guard, instrumented across login/logout, role changes, and every back-office action

solutions.category: A dual-approval workflow could still be raced
items: Wrapped the KYC dual-approval path in an atomic transaction lock so only one approval can commit per case
Added regression tests covering the previously-exploitable approval sequence
Built a self-serve eKYC/IT-Biometrics reporting screen with FAR/FRR/Accuracy tables, year filters, and pagination
Added one-click dynamic Word report generation so compliance no longer compiles figures by hand

achievements.label: Access Control
achievements.value: Replaced ad-hoc permission checks with a single data-driven Role Permission Matrix enforced server-side, closing a dual-approval race condition in the process

achievements.label: Auditability
achievements.value: Every login, permission change, and back-office action now writes an immutable, searchable audit trail entry

achievements.label: Compliance Reporting
achievements.value: Shipped a self-serve eKYC/biometrics accuracy reporting system, replacing manual figure compilation

achievements.label: Longevity
achievements.value: Core back-office platform actively built and maintained since Aug 2024

title: P2P Core Server & API Platform
subtitle: Built and operated the core Django API powering mobile and partner integrations for a regulated P2P lending platform
company: A Bank of Thailand-regulated P2P lending platform

timeline.description: Stood up core contract, StockLend, and re-KYC integration endpoints, then migrated deployment to Gunicorn on App Engine with Docker Compose for local development
Built the investor interest-rate system end to end: Excel-based rate import, contract-time-window matching for tiered rates, and cron jobs to deactivate/reactivate rates as they expire
Upgraded Django from an EOL 5.1 to 5.2 LTS along with 8 dependent packages, closing 10 CVEs including 2 critical SQL injection vulnerabilities
Built the Authorization Matrix data models shared with the back-office platform, then diagnosed and fixed intermittent 500s on the hourly account-balance cron caused by a scaling/timeout mismatch

challenges.title: Interest rates needed time-aware matching, not just current values
challenges.description: Tiered investor interest rates had to be matched against the rate in effect at each contract's creation time, not simply the latest imported rate, or investors could be paid the wrong tier

challenges.title: The framework was running end-of-life with known CVEs
challenges.description: Django 5.1 reached EOL in Dec 2025 while still in production, carrying 10 known CVEs including 2 critical SQL injection issues

challenges.title: A financial cron job intermittently failed
challenges.description: The hourly account-balance reconciliation job would 500 when the scheduler triggered it while the App Engine instance was cold-starting under basic scaling

solutions.category: Interest rates needed time-aware matching, not just current values
items: Reworked the Excel import pipeline to window-match each contract's tier against the rate in effect at its creation time
Added a cron endpoint to deactivate expired rates and a companion fix to reactivate any still-valid rows caught by the sweep

solutions.category: The framework was running end-of-life with known CVEs
items: Upgraded Django 5.1.5 → 5.2.14 LTS and 8 dependent packages in a single coordinated release, closing all 10 outstanding CVEs

solutions.category: A financial cron job intermittently failed
items: Traced the failure to a mismatch between the scaling idle timeout and the Gunicorn process timeout, then capped and aligned both
Found and fixed a cron auth wrapper that was silently swallowing real exceptions as fake success/auth responses, masking the true error

achievements.label: Financial Accuracy
achievements.value: Rebuilt investor interest-rate matching to be time-aware, preventing tier mismatches on rate changes

achievements.label: Security
achievements.value: Closed 10 CVEs (2 critical SQLi) via a coordinated Django LTS upgrade across 8 dependencies

achievements.label: Reliability
achievements.value: Eliminated intermittent 500s on the hourly financial reconciliation cron

achievements.label: Longevity
achievements.value: Core API platform actively built and operated since Aug 2024

company: A Bank of Thailand-regulated P2P lending platform
role: Full Stack Developer & Security Remediation Lead

title: Penetration Testing Vendor Selection
subtitle: Compared 3 vendor bids and selected the best value for a 26 man-day, OWASP Top 10-aligned penetration test
company: A Bank of Thailand-regulated P2P lending platform
role: Full Stack Developer & Security Vendor Evaluation Lead

timeline.description: Requested proposals from 3 penetration testing vendors: Vendor A, Vendor B, and Vendor C
Compared price, test scope (web/mobile function coverage), methodology, and payment terms across all 3 bids
Selected Vendor B for the best combination of test coverage (26 man-days, OWASP Top 10-aligned) and commercial terms
Scope finalized and testing began — see the Security Remediation project for the resulting engagement

challenges.title: Lowest Price Wasn't Best Value
challenges.description: The cheapest bid (Vendor C, ฿417,300) offered the least test coverage of the three, at 16.5 man-days

challenges.title: Vague Scope Language
challenges.description: The most expensive bid (Vendor A, ฿631,300) quoted effort only as "1 month" instead of man-days, making it hard to compare against the others

challenges.title: Cash Flow & Support Trade-offs
challenges.description: Vendors differed sharply on payment terms (installments vs. credit) and on whether post-report support was included

items: Ranked bids by 3 weighted criteria in order: price, test coverage, then additional care
Normalized each quote to a cost-per-man-day figure instead of comparing sticker price alone
Required every vendor to state effort in explicit man-days for an apples-to-apples comparison
Verified each vendor's scope mapped to OWASP Top 10 categories before shortlisting
Selected Vendor B's 45-day credit term, payable only after final delivery, to protect cash flow
Weighted Vendor B's ongoing consulting over a one-off report readout, plus a 10% returning-customer discount

achievements.label: Value
achievements.value: Selected a ฿425,646 bid — 33% below the highest quote (฿631,300) — without sacrificing coverage

achievements.label: Coverage
achievements.value: Secured the most testing effort of the 3 bids: 26 man-days vs. 16.5 (Vendor C) and an unspecified "1 month" (Vendor A)

achievements.label: Terms
achievements.value: Negotiated 45-day credit (payable after final delivery) plus a 10% returning-customer discount

achievements.label: Outcome
achievements.value: Vendor onboarded and testing kicked off on schedule, feeding directly into the Security Remediation project
